397|biur-halacha/part-001.txt|7:א: A shepherd's ox as feet, etc. — see Mishna Berurah; and it is plausible in simplicity that this means specifically a shepherd's ox whose custom is sometimes to sell; therefore we say that even if he sold it on Yom Tov, his intent was from erev Yom Tov to establish it in the domain of whoever will take it afterward, and therefore it is not drawn after the seller's feet. But an ordinary person who does not customarily sell animals — they go after the buyer, since on erev Shabbat it was with him. And in this manner the baraita of Rabbi Dosa on daf 37b is discussed — see there.
397|biur-halacha/part-001.txt|16:_: For the need of his friend, behold they are as the feet of the filler — see Mishna Berurah, which we wrote that there are disputants on this; and we shall explain that in truth the Mechaber's method is according to the words of Rabbeinu Tam and the Rosh and the Ran [also in the chiddushim of the Ra'ah to Beitzah he holds the method of Rabbeinu Tam, except that he is inclined there to say that even as the feet of the filler he speaks, but also as the feet of the one for whom it was filled must be, and the second cannot carry except to a place where both of them made eruv — see there; and his reason is understood according to what he wrote in the chiddushim of the Rashba to challenge the view of Rabbeinu Tam — see in the chiddushim of the Rashba and examine]. But in truth most rishonim disagree on this, and their opinion is that behold they are as the feet of the one for whom it was filled, according to what is established everywhere: one who lifts a found object for his friend — his friend acquires it; and they are Rashi and Rashbam brought in Tosafos, and so ruled R' Chananel in his commentary [and what is brought in the hagahah of Maimonides in the name of R' Chananel is garbled and perhaps there is a textual error there], and so is the opinion of the author of the Ma'or and the Ra'avad there in his hasagot, and so is the opinion of the Rashba in his chiddushim — see there — who extended and challenged the view of Rabbeinu Tam; and so is the Meiri inclined — see there; and so is the opinion of the Maggid, who wrote there that such is the opinion of the Rambam and the Rif, who omitted this halachah because they relied on the known rule that one who lifts a found object for his friend — his friend acquires it [and this reason for the omission of the Rif and the Rambam is more comfortable than the reason of the Ran that they ruled like R' Shimon and relied on the anonymous mishnah that an ox of the Babylonian exiles is as the feet of the filler, and since they did not distinguish in the anonymous case that it deals whether one fills for his own need or for his friend's need — this is a great strain]. And so is the opinion of the Riaz, except that he copied only when we gave it to him and for the reason that he acquires from hefker, and that is only as brought in the sugya of Beitzah; but according to what is established everywhere that one who lifts a found object for his friend — his friend acquires it — we do not need this, and perhaps his intention is also thus, except that he copied as stated in the sugya of Beitzah to Rav Nachman; and so ruled in the method of Rivav in the Alfasi as the feet of the one for whom it was filled, and in Avodat HaKodesh and in Nahar Shalom they commented on almost all the matters, except that they wrote and framed this law as already having come into the hand of the one for whom it was filled; and in truth from all these rishonim it is proven that even while still in the hand of the filler it is likewise forbidden to carry them as his own feet, but as the feet of the one for whom it was filled on his behalf, for behold they are not his but are connected to the one for whom it was filled on his behalf, for one who lifts a found object, etc. — his friend acquires it; and what is written in Avodat HaKodesh that he gave them to his friend is the language of the Gemara, and the same applies even if he did not give, and we did not find this distinction except in the Riaz, and as above he cited for the reason that he acquires from hefker; but for all the rishonim we do not need this but for the reason that one who lifts, etc. — his friend acquires it; and therefore it is plausible to rule not according to the words of the Mechaber but only as the feet of the one for whom it was filled on his behalf, and in particular if they have already reached the hand of the one for whom it was filled — in this it is explicit also in the Riaz; and so too is the opinion of the Bach in such a case that they are as the feet of the one for whom it was filled; and in truth there is more reason to say as the feet of the one for whom it was filled while they are in his hand than while they are still in the hand of the filler — see in the chiddushim of the Rashba in his challenges on the method of Rabbeinu Tam and examine.
397|machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt|9:א: (s.k. 9) Behold, etc. — this is as min b'mino and is not nullified in doubt; but regarding other prohibitions the law is not so — see Peri Chadash Yoreh De'ah siman 102. This matter is discussed in siman 113 below. The Mechaber wrote Magen Avraham there: if it is not recognizable in appearance but only in taste it is nullified even if it came to fix the pot, such as water and salt in dough — end of his words. But this case is different, for these are Magen Avraham's words per Tosafos Beitzah 39a s.v. mishum — they answered first: regarding techumim it is different since they are stringent as min b'mino because it is monetary property; water and salt have other owners like any money and one must nullify the owner's name — this is difficult; therefore they were stringent in doubt. And why did the Mechaber mention water and salt — one may say he cited mishnah language in Beitzah; nevertheless since we have two answers of Tosafos the Mechaber should not mislead — the truth is only when it comes to fix is it not nullified; with Tosafos' first answer, since it is monetary property, but in general not — if so the Mechaber holds only when it comes to fix; with both Tosafos answers together when it is monetary and comes to fix.
398|beur-hagra/part-001.txt|5:ו: And some say — like Rabbi Meir there that the halachah follows the lenient view even when an individual is against the many, as written in Mechaber 35:1; and furthermore Rava holds like him, as written there 32b; and see 27 in the Rosh in the name of the Rambam, and he holds that from what is written it was necessary lest one say, etc. — it teaches us that in every matter the law is so. And it requires study, for if so why did he not rule like every individual against R' Shimon in chapter 4 even fifteen amot; and so too the Rashba there and in Shulchan Aruch HaRav; and also the language does not imply so, but rather according to the Rambam that it teaches us here that the halachah is like R' Yehuda ben Beteira; and so wrote the Rif and Shulchan Aruch.
422|baer-heitev/part-001.txt|2:א: Hallel. And they do not recite it in a house of mourning, for it is said there: "The dead do not praise Hashem" — which would be like mocking the deceased; and see siman 131 s.k. 10 what I wrote there. Women are exempt from all of Hallel because it is a positive time-bound commandment — and Magen Avraham; and see Yad Aharon.
426|biur-halacha/part-001.txt|2:ה: And one blesses standing — in the Gemara it states: Tanna Debei Rabbi Yishmael: were Israel to merit only to receive the countenance of their Father in heaven once a month, it would suffice; Abaye said, etc. And the intent in what he said to receive countenance is that through the moon and the rest of the heavenly host that constantly guard their task we see the greatness of the Holy One blessed be He. And we bless "He who performs truth" upon the Holy One blessed be He, who is a true God whose action is truth — meaning that the action itself is also truth, that it endures forever, as in what is said "and He established them forever." And the principle of blessing is to the Holy One blessed be He alone, and one must not bless or pray to another, heaven forbid, except through the moon His might is seen — and this is receiving the countenance of their Father in heaven [Peri Megadim]. And I heard from someone a reason for what is practiced in many places after kiddush levanah to say "we will praise" — namely so they should not err, heaven forbid, in that we go out toward the moon and rejoice toward it, that there is some concern of a notion that we give honor to the moon; therefore we say "we will praise" and conclude "for Hashem is the God in heaven above," etc. — there is no other; and what we go out for is only to see the might of the Holy One blessed be He, who illuminates at His will to all who come into the world, as in what is said "lift up your eyes on high and see who created these." And it is in the Gemara: Abaye said, therefore one must say it standing; Marimar and Mar Zutra would lean on their servants and bless — see his explanation in the Tur and in Yad Rama to Rabbi Meir HaLevi to tractate Sanhedrin, that because of their old age and heaviness they could not stand and leaned on their servants' shoulders in order to sanctify standing — see there; and it implies from this that in any case leaning for this matter is like standing for one who cannot stand; and see in the chiddushim of Ra'ah in the name of Turei Zahav that it is forbidden to lean then on his staff — and this is when he could stand otherwise.
447|chok-yaakov/part-001.txt|4:ה: Forbidden on Pesach — that is, to drink it; but it is permitted in benefit, all the more so that it is permitted to retain it; so is explained in the responsum of the Rashba siman 174 and in Tur Choshen Mishpat siman 113, who also wrote that everything permitted to retain is permitted to benefit from — see there.
459|chok-yaakov/part-001.txt|1:ו: To send the matzot. And in the responsum of the Rashba siman 124 he wrote that the Rambam sent matzot to the furrier far more than fifteen houses away, and concluded; and in the end he refrained, not because of the furrier's distance but because he feared lest the furrier be full and his bread be delayed outside for the measure of a mil or more; but to be concerned about removal of the hand we did not hear — end of his words; and see what the Mechaber and the Rav wrote in seif 2 in the hagahah.
460|machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt|1:ב: And so wrote the Rashba, etc.: guarding from the time of harvest, etc. — and this is according to the Rif above in siman 453 seif 4; and see there in Peri Chadash that even for blocking. For the Rif, matzah for the mitzvah requires guarding for the sake of the mitzvah from the time of harvest. In the name of the Rashba that even an Israelite on a gentile's dough — and the intent is that if he told him to make it for Pesach it does not help, for the gentile acts according to his own intent.
462|peri-megadim/part-001.txt|1:ב: For — in Yoreh De'ah 126:6 (textual error: 126) — if there is kosher wine in the upper vessel and in the lower vessel, stam yayin is touched: when one pours, the upper remainder is forbidden; and if there is water in it, see as Magen Avraham wrote in letter 2 and Ateret Zekenim letter 2; and in Orach Chayyim 14 there, letter 7, regarding stam yayin of ours there is no need to add water (unless it certainly touched stam yayin); and Eshel Avraham there letter 11: a practical difference in adding water for ours, that it should be nullified in six parts water — see there; and siman 134:65. What Orach Chayyim wrote that se'or and honey disqualify wine — see Yoreh De'ah 123; and Shach letter 8: for ours specifically, if its taste changed it does not forbid in stam yayin — see there.
466|kaf-hachayyim/part-001.txt|4:_: 4) There. One should not chew, etc. — and this is specifically in chewing, for there is no concern of chametzing; and likewise in mere biting; and likewise in mice biting there is no concern of chametzing. Responsum of the Rashba siman 488: R' Abba said, R' Abba said, etc.; and see above siman 453 seif 3; and in our words there b'siyata diShmaya.
468|mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt|10:_: (38) That one should not let blood — for on erev Shavuot it happened that the field whose name is Tavuach came out, and had Israel not accepted the Torah it would have been slaughtered for their flesh and blood; and the rabbis decreed on every erev Yom Tov because of erev Shavuot. And in Ashkenaz they call it "scharfen" or "kepf zetzen"; some permit except for Rosh HaShanah, which is the day of judgment; in any case on erev Shavuot one must be stringent. And on the last erev Yom Tov of Pesach everything is permitted, for it is not a festival in its own right. And all this is when one wishes to let blood for health; but for danger many have already ruled leniently, and "He guards the simple" is Hashem; and even on erev Shavuot the Avnei Nezer permitted when doctors ordered it for an illness involving danger; but otherwise not.
472|kaf-hachayyim/part-001.txt|8:_: 8) There. Until it darkens — that is, tzeit hakochavim. Chayei Adam, general rule 131 in the laws of the order, letter 3; Ben Aharon, portion Tzav, letter 28; Mishna Berurah letter 5; and see below siman 562 seif 1.
467|turei-zahav/part-001.txt|4:_: We are not concerned for an unspecified pile, etc. — so wrote the Rashba in the responsum that the Beit Yosef brought, and so: even those piles that we saw upon which rain fell — we may be lenient with a doubt that perhaps water entered only in the upper sheaves but not in the belly of the pile; and if you say it entered — perhaps it did not have time to chametz, for everything that did not come in water — therefore it is a double doubt for leniency — end of his words. From this too there is a contradiction to the Rama's ruling below, for here it is permitted even for eating.
467|biur-halacha/part-001.txt|14:א: Split wheat — see Taz, who wrote that according to the hagahah above in seif 9, even if it did not split but only softened, this whole seif applies; and so is the opinion of other Acharonim [Bach, Or Sameach, Peri Chadash, article of Mordechai, Gra Zal, Chayei Adam — and not like Shulchan Gavoah who tends to say that in roasting and salting the Rama admits we require splitting; and so Chayei Adam for salting]; except that the Rama relied here on what he wrote in seif 9. And behold, in great loss — such as that he is poor and it is a large important piece, or it prevents joy of Yom Tov — it is implied from the Gra Zal that one may be lenient and rely on the Mechaber's view that peeling a bit suffices; and so Peri Chadash that one may dig deep and discard all around it and it is permitted in eating. And behold, all other Acharonim did not mention in practice this view; but if it softened and did not split, perhaps one may rely on this; and it is possible that the Gra Zal who is lenient in great loss is also specifically when softened; and see in the responsum of the Rama siman 28 — it is proven there that even when softened they practice forbidding that whole piece; and perhaps in great loss he too would agree to be lenient — requires study. And know further that in doubt whether it softened one must not be stringent at all [Acharonim].
467|eshel-avraham/part-001.txt|2:ב: But to eat them. The Taz and Peri Chadash challenged: behold, even for d'oraisa we rely on sefek sefeka, all the more so for d'rabbanan in any amount; see siman 453 seif 3. One must say it deals when there is not sixty against the prohibition — see there until he concludes forbidden to eat them since there is no loss in retaining them; if so, when he has no other grain it is permitted. Shach in Yoreh De'ah wrote the reason: according to Mar Ukva, even if they did not split they are forbidden, and it is sefek sefeka of a dispute, not of reality. According to Chayei Adam siman 7 it is more lenient and he agreed to the Taz — see there. From his words remember what I heard from the mouth of the famous gaon Av Beit Din R' Shaul Narol of Amsterdam, may he live long, some novelties that arose for him in the house of study of Rishon LeTziyon; he preached on what Magen Avraham brought siman 442 s.k. 1: the Tur wrote that every thing not forbidden in eating from the Torah is permitted to mix and retain; and so Semak; but Tosafos at the beginning of Pesachim wrote it is forbidden, for the rabbis did not distinguish, and proved so from the mishnah that se'or must be burned, and although it was stiff and there is no d'oraisa prohibition in eating it, nevertheless it must be burned d'rabbanan, etc.; and according to the Tur that mishnah of se'or must deal with Yom Tov, etc. — end of his words; and it is clear to every discerning eye that this answer is very strained; but in my humble opinion there is room to understand the Tur's method, and on the contrary Tosafos' words need explanation — for Peri Chadash from what R' Gidal said in the name of Rav: one who consecrates from six and above, even in Cordovanian wheat, there is no concern, etc. — see at length; end of his words.
467|magen-avraham/part-001.txt|11:א: The entire dough. So wrote the Rashba siman 176: the wheat kernel did not touch in only one place but here and there through the rolling of the dough; and we say in such a case "here it was found, here it was" (see siman 462). And furthermore, the water in the dough conducts what emerges from that grain throughout the dough; they did not say peeling except dry in dry; and even in a moist place Rav compared it to the place of circumcision at the time of salting; but in a place of gravy they said the gravy conducts even something that does not exude; and likewise bread found in dough — bread is apt to crumble and crumbs mixed in the dough; besides that it itself can chametz others even though baked — except my mind is not inclined that a small thing should chametz the entire dough, etc. — see there; it is proven he holds it forbids even cold — see siman 462.
467|peri-megadim/part-001.txt|10:ד: If they placed the rounds in a bowl and cut and poured gravy and found a softened wheat kernel — one may say to forbid the pouring; and all the more they are stringent when there was not the measure of a mil in hot food there is no measure. And even though already cooked in fat, perhaps it was not cooked well; and all the more if they cut the wheat and found white flour — behold we saw it was not cooked well; and see siman 463 in Magen Avraham letter 4. And in the introduction we challenged from Pesachim 39b: cooked chametzes and we do not establish it in fruit juice; afterward in water it does not chametz; and according to Rashi that stiff is fine; and responsum of the Ran siman 59 — one may say such a case is fruit juice and water; and one may say stiff is nullified in sixty; and it will be explained in letter 21 on this.
467|peri-megadim/part-001.txt|14:א: Forbidden — Orach Chayyim, Magen Avraham letter 16, and Chayei Adam: from time to time we establish prohibition, but from place to place we do not establish prohibition. And in the Tur: an incident where they peeled, etc., and our Rabbi Ra'avan forbade — see there — and he did not mention splitting; and the Mechaber to his method in seif 9: specifically in splitting; if not split but softened, even in kli rishon in any amount the dish is permitted; and the explanation is before boiling, before they boiled the chicken (not cold, and from place to place we do not establish prohibition); and so one may reconcile the words of the Taz with Magen Avraham to distinguish between time and place; and see letters 16 and 17; and it will be explained there further. And the Taz wrote: one should not challenge — behold it is a double doubt (textual error in some editions): perhaps it fell now and perhaps it was digested in the chicken; one may say in a whole wheat kernel even if split it is not digested. And what he wrote "perhaps it did not chametz" is difficult, for in splitting the Mechaber wrote and it is certainly chametz for us — and so in letter 15. And it is possible likewise for us: even softened is forbidden in peeling — why is it a double doubt; and one may answer that doubt of lack of wisdom is not in the category of doubt; nevertheless in letter 15 he permitted selling for us when softened through double doubt as this; but in one doubt when softened he forbids benefit — not like Chayei Adam, as written in letter 14 from this.
466|chok-yaakov/part-001.txt|4:א: Water fell on the flour. And similarly the Bach is stringent in siman 453 also regarding flour from which mice ate; but if they only bit the sack and there is room to doubt that perhaps they ate nothing of the flour — even if found during Pesach one may permit retaining it. And in the responsum of Maharam of Lublin siman 119 he is somewhat lenient regarding sacks gnawed by mice in time of distress — see there. Also the Taz permits to take around the bitten place and the rest he will sift and eat on Pesach even if dried — end of his words. And Magen Avraham wrote: and in my humble opinion regarding mice one must be more stringent, for these mice are wicked — they go throughout the sack and eat; and all the more when placed in barrels, for then it certainly goes throughout the flour; therefore the above geonim were stringent; and so in Mabit to be stringent for this reason — see there. And in my humble opinion it appears one need not be stringent at all regarding mice that ate flour, and to permit through sifting in every case, because the essential law of flour that mice ate was not mentioned at all in any early posek — only the Acharonim learned this law from wheat kernels that mice bit, for we establish as one who says mouse spittle chametzes, as explained above siman 453. And in my humble opinion: even though mouse spittle chametzes, nevertheless in their eating from flour there is no concern of chametzing at all; and clear proof to this from the mishnah in chapter 9 of Parah mishnah 3: all creeping things that drank water of purification do not disqualify, because no saliva emerges from their mouths except the weasel — R' Eliezer says also the mouse; and the halachah is not like R' Eliezer, as the Rambam, Rashi, and Ra'avad wrote; and so the Rambam explicitly chapter 9 laws of Parah law 12 that no moisture emerges from its mouth; and so Tosafos first chapter of Chullin. Behold that even liquids apt to receive moisture nevertheless do not disqualify; all the more flour where each crumb is separate from its fellow — there is no concern at all that it becomes moist from what it does not eat. And one should not compare to wheat kernels that are one mass and because of the strength of the bite we are concerned that some moisture remained from what remained of the kernel — not so in flour, where one may be lenient in every case; and this is clear. But my mind is not decisive against the great Acharonim, and in particular since they are stringent and I am lenient; nevertheless one may permit to tie the bitten place and permit the rest in every case through sifting, as the Taz ruled; and one who is stringent in this did not consider its thinness. And all this when one does not see any moistness in the bitten place; but if one sees any moistness in the bitten place, one may attribute it to a common matter — perhaps the mice urinated on the flour; and see below s.k. 14 whether there is concern of chametzing from urine, and it is as if moistened with water.
447|peri-megadim/part-001.txt|1:ז: And after consideration I saw that what the Mechaber wrote in Yoreh De'ah 134:2 regarding small barrels being nullified — these are clear matters for halachah; and Pesach is different, for they made several stringencies from what is written: dry in dry is not nullified. And not as the Rashba wrote in Teshuvot HaRosh kvav and in responsum to the Mechaber, and also that we do not follow after the reason. And proof to this from what is written in Pesachim 43a: Rava said the halachah is chametz in its time in its kind and not in its kind in any amount like Rav — it implies certainly that Rav literally holds so; and although not for his reason, nevertheless in the substance of the law he holds like Rav; and now for Rav in its kind in any amount — for Rav also in dry, as Rabbeinu Tam wrote after retraction (see Tosafos Menachot 22 s.v. from here, etc.) (and what we learned that terumah in 101 is nullified in ordinary food that is fixed — see there); and Rav decreed not in its kind lest in its kind — the same applies in dry; Rava also holds thus. And although we have no ruling that the Mechaber would hold thus — in 447:64 and 461 and 453 in Magen Avraham 6: flour in flour is called wet in wet — therefore there is no proof from Beitzah 38b for R' Yehuda that wheat in wheat is not nullified — one may say it deals with flour; and see Tosafos Menachot and Yevamot chapter HaOrlah from this; and seemingly on the contrary there is contradiction to this from what the Mechaber wrote in Tur Choshen Mishpat general 45:6 and in Mechaber Choshen Mishpat 10 who gave a reason for doubt and did not give the Ran's reason brought in Taz Yoreh De'ah 102:5 and his praise because dry in dry in doubt should be nullified. Nevertheless I say the Mechaber from his own reasoning was stringent in chametz since he said in any amount like Rav and holds like Rabbeinu Tam and because of the stringency of chametz; and the halachah is like one view, and as we need to say below it will be explained; and see there he wrote dry in dry is not nullified in its kind specifically of doubt; and it is difficult — for the Rambam even not in its kind holds the reason in chametz because of doubt in chapter 13:13 in Magen Avraham; and Eshel Avraham Yoreh De'ah 102:14 — one may say here that one says dry is nullified in any amount and all hold chametz of doubt, and in its kind not like the Rambam, and not in its kind in wet in any amount because of karet and we do not dismiss; and one may say also the words of Or Sameach are thus; and it will be explained inside.
451|eliyah-rabbah/part-001.txt|5:_: And if they filled, etc. This is the language of the Beit Yosef from the Rashba in Torat HaBayit; it seems he did not have the text in the Gemara "and if it is full, gomeri, it is fine," for he wrote: and if in a vessel whose way is not to kindle from inside like a pot, even if they kindled from inside it is forbidden lest one attribute; and if he returned it to the furnace it is permitted — until here. And the same applies to a portable oven whose way is not to kindle from inside; and it is possible the Rashba agrees regarding the portable oven since it is made of bricks and clay — until here the language of the Beit Yosef. And in Chok Yaakov he extended to wonder why the Beit Yosef wondered on the Rashba — behold this distinction of the portable oven is proven at the end of the siman where it says if full gomeri it is permitted — see there. And it is not difficult, for since the Rashba did not bring the law of full gomeri there, it entered his mind that he did not have that text; and furthermore in the Gemara one may say that also in pots it is permitted when full gomeri as he wrote; and in Machilot Kevodo he saw only Torat HaBayit page 46, but it was omitted on page 33 that he ruled explicitly permitted when filled with coals; also in the long Torat HaBayit of the Rashba page 83 he did not see, where he copied the Gemara "and if full gomeri it is fine" and reads like our Gemara; also one may wonder on him, for it is clear explicitly to the Rashba there that he permits even in a pottery portable oven when full gomeri; and so implies Shulchan Aruch and Levush who wrote "and so a small oven called padila," etc., and it is a pottery vessel as Beit Yosef wrote at the beginning of siman 461; and so I proved in my books to Yoreh De'ah beginning siman 97 from Tosafos Pesachim daf 30: if not so, what do they challenge on that portable oven that is permitted when full gomeri — behold the Torah testified about a pottery vessel that it never leaves its impurity — see there: behold the portable oven deals with bricks and clay; but perforce it is reasonable that it deals with pottery; and so explained the Rambam chapter 5 laws of chametz. Also I wondered from this on the Bach here who wrote in the name of Tosafos the opposite, that it deals with bricks and clay. And that which is established for us that kindling from outside does not help — one may say specifically pots, for he is concerned, which is not so in a portable oven that he is not concerned even of pottery; and so is explained in Rokeach end of siman 484; and all this I wrote briefly in Eliyahu Zuta. Also one may say that full gomeri that the Gemara permits applies also to pots: specifically for mere kindling we say he is concerned, which is not so when full gomeri — we see he is not concerned and it is like returning to the furnace; and so appears the view of Magen Avraham and so implies in Tosafos there; and so is explained explicitly in Pesakim Tosafot chapter Kol She'ah siman 88; and all this is not like Shibolei Leket and the tanna who explained full gomeri permitted — it deals specifically with an oven kindled from inside.
462|peri-megadim/part-001.txt|1:א: What the Mechaber wrote: fruit juice with water chametzes faster than other dough — it implies it is complete chametz according to Rambam; and in Tur it is written it becomes stiff; fruit juice with water — if it stood idle for the measure of a mil, at least; and so too Rosh z"l Pesachim 35a (1) that stiff it is; and chametzed (Rambam); and as Tosafos wrote there s.v. fruit juice — and thus the language implies "they are not liable for karet" — but lashes according to Rambam; and although Tur in 442 wrote the conclusion of the Rosh is like the Rif that stiff is d'rabbanan — one must say two types of stiff — strained; and Peri Chadash here. And Rambam chapter 5 Choshen Mishpat 2 implies fruit juice with water is complete chametz literally and karet too one is liable; nevertheless there, dough kneaded in fruit juice — they are not liable for karet; likewise there is no prohibition in it and we do not establish it through water either — we learn from water karet too one is liable. And I thought to say the rejection of Magen Avraham from what he wrote in chapter 6 Choshen Mishpat likewise wine and milk and honey and olive oil eighteen — it is rich matzah; and other fruit juice goes out with water that is not rich matzah — behold without water olive oil does not come to chametz; and therefore with water according to Rambam it is forbidden, for if stiff still there is no eighteen — why do I need bread of affliction. But Rambam z"l chapter 4 Choshen Mishpat 11 in garments washed in milk — it implies stiff for him is also a prohibition; nevertheless there that the form of chametz does not stand; nevertheless chapter 5 Choshen Mishpat mishnah of others implies red vinegar is complete chametz through mixtures; and he holds it chametzes in water with wine; and see Tosafos 35b s.v. fruit juice — it implies fruit juice with water karet too one is liable; and Peri Chadash. And therefore kneading dough water with fruit juice and doubt that it stood the measure of a mil — requires study, for one should not make a rabbinic doubt; and likewise for one who says stiff is nullified in sixty — Magen Avraham 447:5 requires study here, for it appears from Rambam and the sealed language of the Mechaber that he chametzed according to Rambam; and necessarily two types of stiff; but since there is no karet one may say nullified in sixty; and therefore ground matzah that they fried in fat and a wheat kernel was found inside — even though there is salt from our water — one may say it is stiff and nullified in sixty; and it will be explained below further on this. And see Menachot 54a: an apple they crushed, etc., and he concludes stiff it is; and for what Tosafos wrote fruit juice with water, etc. — we learn stiff it is and not karet; and Magen Avraham 1; and it will be explained there one may say it deals with a sour sharp apple and not water is stiff; and Peri Chadash.
442|chok-yaakov/part-001.txt|1:ד: And all similar things — namely red vinegar and Egyptian olives, all those listed in the mishnah at the beginning of Elu Overin; and also yayin sharaf made from sour grain called maltz, as written in the responsum of Magen Avraham siman 58 that it is complete chametz and worse than a mixture of chametz — see there: a matter in its taste; and so too Maharam in Tikatin in a printed responsum at the beginning of the Rif Krakow edition in Seder Nashim — see there; and there is no distinction between that made from sour grain or that made from beer leaven — and not as occurred to one wise person, as I will copy his question to me in his name. And thus: The question: I asked one matter and I ask His Excellency to answer me on an incident that came to me while I was in Ashkenaz. I was asked about Reuven who had yayin sharaf made from barley beer leaven; he forgot to sell before Pesach, and during the festival it was remembered that he did not sell it; and the yayin sharaf was in a gentile's house — the aforementioned Israelite had a room in the gentile's house — and I was asked the law of the yayin sharaf, which is a great loss worth about two hundred reichstaler. And behold, according to the quick view it is a simple law to forbid, for it is chametz on which Pesach passed and must be burned — from what we learned in the Gemara daf 42: and these transgress on Pesach: Babylonian kotach and Median beer, etc.; and Rashi explained these transgress in bal yera'eh and bal yimatzei; and so Riva; and the Rosh wrote in the name of Rabbeinu Tam: specifically Median beer in which they put barley; but our beer made in Ashkenaz whose essence is from barley is complete chametz and has a kezayit in the measure of eating a peras; and so the Tur and all Acharonim; and the same in yayin sharaf made from grain — it is complete chametz prohibition with a kezayit in kedei achilat peras; and so ruled all Acharonim; and so is established that yayin sharaf is chametz and not as one who says it is mere sweat; and therefore in our case it is chametz on which Pesach passed and forbidden in benefit. But it appears to me to side some permission and save Jewish money; and it appears to divide between yayin sharaf made from grain and that made from leaven: since we establish like Rabbeinu Tam in Elu Overin — from the table, for they are not fit to eat; but in bal yera'eh and bal yimatzei there is no mixture of chametz; and in Tur siman 442 it states: all these to R' Eliezer are in a prohibition and have no karet; according to him forbidden to retain; and to the rabbis even a prohibition they have only a general prohibition; according to them permitted to retain; and so the Rif and Rosh; and so is established. And according to what is in the Gemara Bava Batra 96b: the rabbis taught: one date beer, one barley, one wine leaven — one blesses on them shehakol; others say leaven that has taste of wine — one blesses borei peri hagafen; and we establish the halachah is like the first tanna. Further there R' Nachman asked R' Chiya: leaven that has taste of wine — what? Rashi explained: he asks about wine blessing; and a baraita was not heard by him — if so it should have said halachah like others or not — end Rashi. And he answered him: who thought it is wine? It is mere kivui — end; and Tosafot wrote: who thought it is wine? It is mere kivui — from here R' Chananel ruled b'dieved if a gentile washed wine-leaven barrels it is permitted — it is not wine but mere kivui — end; and so Tosafos s.v. leaven of terumah: for all matters it is only mere kivui; only in consecrated they were stringent — see there; and so in Asheri in the name of R' Yonah — see there; if so, likewise regarding chametz one may be lenient since it is only mere kivui. And one should not say to be more stringent with leaven than grain because it is a davar ha'me'amed u'machmitz even in a thousand not nullified — this is not so if one puts leaven in the dough or honey to make a drink for chametz — that is forbidden, as in responsum of Maharam Lublin — to exclude here where they put nothing in the leaven except mere moisture that emerges from the leaven, which is really only mere sweat, as in Tosafos chapter HaMocher daf 62 s.v. one date beer — see there. And leaven that is only kivui is not better than the agent in leaf-serf whose essence is permitted as in first chapter of Orlah and as in Gemara Avodah Zarah 34 and 35; and certainly they do not have a kezayit in kedei achilat peras; and the Tur wrote in the name of the Rosh in siman 442: everything not practiced except for mere kivui — permitted to retain until after Pesach; and even though we establish one blesses on wine leaven in pa'ah — as in Orach Chayyim — see there; in Beit Yosef he answered on the sugya in Bava Batra: behold it states there in bal yera'eh — it deals specifically with their wines that were strong — to exclude our wines; all the more beer leaven — see there. And further, since the incident was inadvertent and he forgot to sell, one should not penalize like R' Shimon who penalizes after Pesach, as in the Ran this reasoning regarding mixture of chametz; and further it appears to side permission since he nullified his chametz and hefker helps b'shogeg as in Avodat HaKodesh in the name of Maharam of Recanti; and although already challenged on this in responsum of Magen Avraham — see there — truth the law is so that this nullification does not help when he said all my chametz while his heart was not with him; even so in our case b'shogeg it appears it helps, as in Tur siman 431: from the Torah general nullification suffices; and as above, except the sages required removal from the house, etc.; and although the Rambam wrote it is d'oraisa, the Beit Yosef already challenged and we conclude it is d'rabbanan and permitted to retain on Pesach; and all the more the yayin sharaf was not in a Jewish house. And although we establish one who deposits chametz with a gentile — the Israelite transgresses bal yera'eh and bal yimatzei — here is different since he nullified his chametz and it is also only kivui; therefore it appeared from all these reasons to permit in benefit at least. And afterward one sage showed me responsum of Maharam Tikatin printed at the beginning of Seder Nashim to the Rif, and there it says to forbid whether from sour grain or beer leaven; but one may distinguish in our case: there the sage ruled l'chatchila to retain yayin sharaf in his house — unlike our case where it was b'shogeg and also not in a Jewish house; therefore it appears permitted; and the great rabbi R' Shmuel Av Beit Din of Frieda agreed with me because of some sides of permission I wrote and great loss, on a double condition that another of the teachers also agree — otherwise his words are void; thus instruct us your view on this — said the humble Meir son of AA Moharar Moshe called R' Meir R' Kaplans of Pozna. Answer: although my mind is not decisive, and especially in the strict law of chametz prohibition — and I, Yaakov, am a worm — how shall I open my mouth where great ones stand, vessels of precious speech who already ascended mountains and descended valleys; to Beit Pamiel she raised and agreed with him in reason and knowledge; but in order not to return a blank face I said to remove the veil of shame from my face, and God is our God for salvations, and give truth to Yaakov, and not come, heaven forbid, to error; and this came out first. Behold what your honor wrote as a side for permission: since we establish like Rabbeinu Tam that bal yera'eh and bal yimatzei do not apply to mixture of chametz, etc. — I do not know how this reasoning is simple to him, for behold in Shulchan Aruch siman 442 he ruled explicitly that one transgresses a prohibition on mixture of chametz even without a kezayit in kedei achilat peras, for he listed Babylonian kotach that has no kezayit in kedei achilat peras as explicitly in the Gemara: leave Babylonian kotach that has no kezayit; and if he roasted and ate (meaning they ate together without dipping) his mind is voided to everyone; and even though one may say nevertheless it deals with eating it in one sitting kedei achilat peras — therefore obligated to burn it; and what the Gemara says if he roasted and ate his mind is voided — this means his mind is voided and the tanna does not deal with this; but if it happened he ate so they are liable on it; and so in responsum Maharam of Trani siman 246 in the name of R' Yosef Beit Rav; and you will find this explanation also in Tosafot Nazir — see there; nevertheless the sealed language of Shulchan Aruch implies that in every matter one is liable on mixture of chametz even without kezayit in kedei achilat peras; and so agree all Acharonim (and when I looked at this law in rishonim and acharonim who extended greatly in these laws, I saw a standing and great wonder in the words of the Taz in the beginning of siman 442 wondering on the Beit Yosef who wrote that for the rabbis even though they do not transgress on mixture of chametz in the prohibition of bal yera'eh, nevertheless forbidden to retain from bal yimatzei; and the Taz wrote: and further wonder greatly on him why he establishes the mishnah of Elu Overin like R' Eliezer who holds there is a prohibition in this — why not establish the mishnah even like the rabbis — behold the mishnah does not teach lashes but transgresses; and Rashi: transgresses from the world; and it fits well like the rabbis that there is in it in any case a prohibition when they exist in the world even though there is no lashes — end Taz; and I do not know how this mishnah that teaches explicitly behold these are in a warning, proving there is a prohibition in its removal, and it does not come like the rabbis at all, was hidden from him; and on this the Gemara says there and there is not even a slight difficulty on the Beit Yosef). And further: even if we say in mixture of chametz we require kezayit in kedei achilat peras, nevertheless here in yayin sharaf it is not called mixture of chametz but chametz literally like the leaven themselves — sweat emerging from the beverage as beverage, as proven from many mishnayot in chapters 2 and 5 of Machshirin and chapter 25, and as explained in responsum of the Rosh general 20 siman 26 and in Ribash siman 295 — see there; and so explicitly in responsum Magen Avraham siman 58 that yayin sharaf made from chametz is chametz literally and not mixture of chametz — see there; and so in responsum Maharam Tikatin that it is considered prohibition in its essence and is a davar ha'me'amed and not mere sweat — see there. But what your honor raised to distinguish and say that specifically yayin sharaf from sour grain has concern of prohibition unlike that from leaven, because the leaven themselves are kivui as established in the Gemara Bava Batra — behold even though seemingly this division is correct, even though there is stringency for stam yayin and also for blessing, nevertheless one may distinguish and say for our case it was only kivui as the meaning of the Gemara and Tosafos there s.v. likewise he clarified from its measure, etc., and s.v. who thought — see there: I wonder from the outset of the law: from where did he come to compare beer leaven to wine leaven, which have no relation at all, as sense and intellect testify — certainly wine leaven: the wine itself is the clear thing and leaven comes only from waste of stones and dregs that settled below and have no taste except kivui; not so beer leaven that as soon as they receive chametz taste they are clear, and leaven comes from the mash and wheat and barley that were ground and settled below — they are the essence of chametz in taste and appearance and chametz most doughs in them, and they have only kivui of the beer, but they themselves are the essence of chametz and flour. And also what your honor tends to leniency because it was in a gentile's house — for according to many poskim one does not transgress bal yera'eh and bal yimatzei — behold from the wording of the question your honor wrote it implies the Jew had a rented room in the gentile's house, and if so it is as his own; and further that some poskim hold no transgression in bal yera'eh and bal yimatzei if in a gentile's house — that is if the gentile accepted responsibility; not so without accepting responsibility, and it is simple as explained in Beit Yosef end of siman 440 — see there; and your honor is silent whether he accepted responsibility. And because it was b'shogeg one may not be lenient at all, for chametz on which Pesach passed, whether b'shogeg or ones, is forbidden in benefit as explained in siman 448. And what your honor wrote on the law of nullification before witnesses — I did not wish to write from this, as I already explained this law in Torat HaShleimim printed in question 16; why should I repeat, for all parts of the answer are explained there — thus the words of the small one Yaakov.
442|chokhmat-shlomo/part-001.txt|1:_: Seif 1. Mixture of chametz — one transgresses on it, etc. Note: behold in the law that permission joins to prohibition — such as when a minority of permission mixed in a majority of prohibition — if one is lashed for a kezayit of the permission and prohibition together; and see in my chiddushim to tractate Niddah daf 27b regarding perhaps two peridos would not be abundant — a revi'it on a perida of dust and its measure increases; and there I proved that also the minority permission joins the majority for impurity of the house; and the same for prohibition — on this the questioner and answerer there will disagree — see there and examine. And behold, see the language of the Beit Yosef in this siman who wrote in the name of Maggid Mishneh on our rabbi's words in this language: a contradiction appears in the language of the book from itself to itself, etc., with the end; and before I answer — behold this language is not understood, and also the body of his answer has no understanding. And it appears there is a textual error here, and first it must read: and before I answer I shall precede, for the reason the Mechaber distinguished, etc.; and his intent in this introduction settles the first difficulty: although he brought first that retaining is one degree lighter than eating, he afterward brings the Rambam's language that one transgresses bal yera'eh on mixtures — because first the Tur goes in the method of the commentators that Elu Overin means from the table; and for this explanation one may say retaining is lighter than eating on one side; but the Rambam who explains Elu Overin as bal yera'eh — therefore he holds the law of removal and eating are literally equal, and the first wonder is removed; and afterward it must read: and what is possible to explain in permission — contradiction two — namely he now comes to settle the second difficulty: namely what the Rambam ruled like the sages is for eating, but for bal yera'eh he ruled like the sages and for him removal is stricter than eating — and this is per the explanation of the Ramach; and therefore for transgressing bal yera'eh even without kezayit in kedei achilat peras, but for eating one is not lashed without kedei achilat peras — and with this he concludes; and thus the two contradictions I mentioned will be resolved: namely the first contradiction was resolved in the first introduction and the second in this introduction. So appears the intent of the Maggid Mishneh; without this his words have no understanding — examine; and see in Magen Avraham s.k. 1 what he wrote on mixtures of chametz, etc.; and Kessef Mishneh agreed to the second view. And behold the Beit Yosef explained the matter more: for bal yera'eh the Rambam ruled like R' Eliezer since the anonymous mishnah is like him — namely since in any case the chametz is in his house; but for eating the Rambam ruled like the sages. And I was asked by one man: if so, who pressed the Gemara to say the mishnah is like R' Eliezer — behold one may say it comes even like the rabbis, and they disagree only on eating but on removal they agree. And I answered: there is room, for the beginning of the mishnah one may say the intent is for bal yera'eh as Rashi; as a mishnah in any case the ending that concludes behold these are in a warning and have no karet — perforce deals with eating, as Rashi himself: if for bal yera'eh why conclude and have no karet — behold even chametz in its essence has no karet for bal yera'eh; and why does it teach us this in mixtures; also from the Torah it would be reasonable to say there should be karet in bal yera'eh and bal yimatzei — perforce it deals with eating. Therefore from the ending one must say it comes like R' Eliezer; and specifically the beginning is considered anonymous since he cited anonymous first it is anonymous; but the ending behold these in a warning is not anonymous — one may say this is the conclusion of R' Eliezer's words, for R' Eliezer spoke first in the mishnah: R' Eliezer says also women's ornaments — and everything after this is R' Eliezer's words; therefore not considered anonymous; therefore the Rambam ruled here like the sages; and so it is; and simple in my humble opinion — examine. And what Magen Avraham wrote there in the name of the Rashba that everything one intends to make so is not nullified — see what I wrote on it in my compositions Orach Chayyim year 5601 in chiddushim to Pesachim chapter 2 on the sugya one does not cook the Pesach offering in water — see there what he wrote to wonder on it greatly — examine there; and see what I further wrote on these words of Magen Avraham; and in Yoreh De'ah siman 134 he wrote in the name of the Rashba, etc., and we wrote to settle his difficulty in my compositions Orach Chayyim year 5627 in my answer to the community Stanislav — it bought its place in omissions to Sefer HaChaim to Kontras Minei Mitamim — see there what I wrote — examine. And behold see in Magen Avraham s.k. 1 what he wrote: the Maggid Mishneh wrote chapter 4: specifically when there is a kezayit of chametz within kedei achilat peras — this is the essence; and the second view: although one does not transgress by eating, one is obligated in removal; and although mixed in many olives one transgresses, for behold there is a kezayit of chametz there; and Kessef Mishneh agreed to the second view — end Magen Avraham. And behold in my opinion it appears to decide [like the view] of Kessef Mishneh from the Yerushalmi first chapter of Beitzah halachah 2: on the mishnah Beit Shammai say se'or in a kezayit, etc.; and thus: R' Avahu in the name of R' Yochanan — whether in its removal or in eating — a kezayit; R' Mana argued with R' Chizkiya; he said to him: yes; Rav heard this matter; he said: from R' Avahu; he said: and we too say R' Avahu in the name of R' Yochanan — whether for removal or eating a kezayit; if not so, thirty-seven karetot would be taught in the Torah — end. And behold this Yerushalmi is like the signed book; and the Kaf HaChayyim made a textual error and it must read: whether in removal whether in eating — in a kotevet. And behold besides the difficulty of corrupting the books, its explanation is also wondrous: one — that he himself wondered on the measures of offerings — what difficulty, perhaps it comes not like Beit Shammai; and I wonder more: even without his proof there that the mishnah would not be like all, even if we say it is like all — if it were a matter he could teach according to all it would be difficult why he put it in dispute — he should teach what is like all; but here behold if there would be thirty-seven karetot for inadvertence it would only be like Beit Shammai not Beit Hillel; if so in the end it would be like the tannaim — why abandon Beit Hillel's words and teach like Beit Shammai. And further wonder: behold there in Keritot they did not list measures but species — for what is one liable karet and chatat; if so behold one counts and eats chametz — what difference if one eats a kezayit chametz or two olives; if so he could teach that one ate several olives of chametz; and perforce he did not teach only the species; if so likewise what difference chametz or se'or, and what matter that this is kezayit and that in a kotevet. And strained to say since they disagree in oil and in judgment to Beit Shammai therefore he had to count them — this is strained to challenge thus — what difficulty. Therefore the text appears in its simplicity; and the answer is according to what I wrote in my chiddushim to laws of Pesach siman 431, and it is in my compositions Orach Chayyim year 5629 page 40 in explanation of Yerushalmi language in chapter 5 of Pesachim; and what emerges: that Beit Hillel hold both in a kezayit; and the Gemara explains the reason we learn removal from eating — the intent is not by way of mah matzinu, for certainly there is no proof, for eating is stricter; only the intent is by way of kal va'chomer: Beit Hillel hold therefore in all measures kezayit because the extra language is that the language of eating is kezayit; and automatically where eating is not written it should be kal va'chomer; and if so in removal, since eating is not written, it should be kal va'chomer; only we learn a leniency from eating, and a leniency is properly learned from eating by way of kal va'chomer; and since from kal va'chomer we learn removal from eating, we require also in removal a measure; automatically it is reasonable to say sufficient to come from the law to be like the case; therefore also in removal kezayit — see there where I extended on this. And behold the novelty here is in the dispute of Kessef Mishneh and Maggid Mishneh: we learn removal from eating in mah matzinu — if so reasonable to say argue from it and establish in its place: granted in eating if not in kedei achilat peras one does not eat together; but in removal, since in the end the chametz is in his house — all the more if by kal va'chomer — if so likewise sufficient from the law to be like the case; and since in eating one is liable only if mixed in kedei achilat peras — the same in removal. And this is the intent of the Yerushalmi: behold if we say we learn removal from eating in mah matzinu — difficult, we should also learn for karet to be liable on bal yera'eh; and one should not say the truth is so, for behold in mishnah Elu Overin it teaches behold these in a warning and have no karet; but from this alone is no proof, for one may say there it deals when there is no kezayit in kedei achilat peras — then one should not learn from eating, for in eating too one is exempt in such a case. And it would be that we say argue from it and establish in its place: one transgresses even if not in kedei achilat peras — from a place; if we say establish in its place — behold in it karet is not said, only a prohibition; but when it is within kedei achilat peras in a matter where in eating one is liable for karet — one may say also in removal one is liable. Therefore the Yerushalmi said this is impossible to say, for if so it should teach thirty-seven karetot also in removal when in kedei achilat peras; and perforce in removal in every case exempt from karet; and perforce we do not learn in mah matzinu removal from eating, only by kal va'chomer; and automatically sufficient from the law to be like the case; and one does not transgress bal yera'eh except in kedei achilat peras; and this is what the Yerushalmi said: whether in removal whether in eating kezayit — namely we require kezayit together in kedei achilat peras; and proof that perforce Beit Hillel who learn removal from eating is perforce by kal va'chomer, for he said in mah matzinu — if so to obligate karet also on removal; and one should not say the truth is so that one is liable if in kedei achilat peras; and the mishnah that teaches behold these in a warning deals with more than kedei achilat peras — if so it should teach thirty-seven karetot; and it fits well with R' Eliezer. And behold further proof to our words from what the Sma wrote in Choshen Mishpat beginning siman 72: according to the majority the latter bin is simpler than the first; and if we emend like the Kaf HaChayyim's text whether in removal whether in eating in a kotevet — then the first bin would be simpler; and strained to emend also this that in reverse it should teach whether in eating whether in removal in a kotevet — this too is strained to emend; and perforce as I wrote — examine well.
